Kuvitus: talvinen maantie kaartaa metsän: Illustration: a winter road curves to the right through a forest and disappears far away behind hills. In the middle of the bend a car is driving, seen from behind. There are snowbanks and spruce trees at the sides of the road.
Kaksi kuvaa. Vasemmalla kappale kiertää: Two pictures. On the left an object goes round a circular path anticlockwise at a steady speed. At two points in the upper part of the path the blue velocity arrows v 1 and v 2 are along the tangent of the path; the arrows are equally long but point in different directions. At the topmost point between them the orange acceleration arrow a n points straight down to the centre of the path. On the right the same velocity arrows are drawn from the same point. The arrow between the tips of the arrows, the change of velocity delta v, points straight down, that is in the same direction as the acceleration, towards the centre of the path. The velocity arrows are equally long in both pictures, at the same scale.
Kaksi kuvaa. Vasemmalla tilannekuva ylhä: Two pictures. On the left a view from above: the road curves to the left and the car is in the bend. The centre of the bend is on the left, and the dashed line r joins it to the car. Beside the car the blue velocity arrow v points up along the road and the orange acceleration arrow a n points left towards the centre. On the right the free-body diagram of the car seen from behind, the car drawn as a rectangle on the road: the weight G from the centre downwards, the support force N of the road from the bottom face upwards and equally long, and the friction force of the road from the left corner of the bottom face to the left towards the centre of the bend, about half the length of the weight. Separately the orange acceleration arrow a n to the left.
Kuvaaja mittakaavassa: vaaka-akselilla r: Graph to scale: on the horizontal axis the tangential speed v in metres per second from zero to 30, on the vertical axis the centripetal acceleration a n in metres per second squared from zero to 18. Two orange curves rise from the origin ever more steeply. For a radius of 50 metres the solid curve: at a speed of 10 the acceleration is 2, at 20 it is 8 and at 30 it is 18. For a radius of 100 metres the dashed curve is half as high: at a speed of 20 the acceleration is 4 and at 30 it is 9. The points at speeds 10 and 20 are marked on the solid curve with guide lines.
Neljä kuvaa kahdessa sarakkeessa. Vasemm: Four pictures in two columns. Top left a car at the top of a hill, top right a car at the bottom of a dip; in both the car drives to the right at the same speed. Below each is the free-body diagram of the car, the car drawn as a rectangle: the weight G from the centre downwards and the support force N of the road from the bottom face upwards. At the top of the hill the support force is shorter than the weight, about six tenths of it, and the orange acceleration arrow a n points down, towards the centre of the arc of the hill. At the bottom of the dip the support force is longer than the weight, about 1.4 times, and the acceleration arrow points up, towards the centre of the arc of the dip. The weight is equally long in both.
Auton voimakuvio takaa katsottuna, auto: Free-body diagram of the car seen from behind, the car drawn as a rectangle on the road. The centre of the bend is on the right. The weight G from the centre downwards, the support force N of the road from the bottom face upwards and equally long, and the friction force of the road from the right corner of the bottom face to the right towards the centre of the bend, about half the length of the weight. Separately the orange acceleration arrow a n to the right. In the corner the axes: x to the right towards the centre and y up.
Opiskelijan piirtämä voimakuvio autosta,: A free-body diagram of a car going over the top of a hill, drawn by a student; the car is a rectangle. From the centre an arrow G straight down. From the bottom face an arrow N straight up, shorter than G. From the middle of the top face an arrow F cf straight up. Together the arrows N and F cf are as long as G.
Auton voimakuvio, auto suorakulmiona. Pa: Free-body diagram of the car, the car drawn as a rectangle. The weight G from the centre downwards and the support force N from the bottom face upwards; the support force is about one and a half times as long as the weight.
Free-body diagram of the car, the car drawn as a rectangle. The weight G from the centre downwards and the support force N from the bottom face upwards; the arrows are equally long.

Free-body diagram of the car, the car drawn as a rectangle. The weight G from the centre downwards and the support force N from the bottom face upwards; the support force is about half the length of the weight.

Free-body diagram of the car, the car drawn as a rectangle. The weight G from the centre downwards, the support force N from the bottom face upwards about one and a half times the length of the weight, and from the bottom face downwards an arrow F cf, half the length of the weight.
Mallikuvio: jääkiekko liukuu narun varas: Model diagram: an ice hockey puck slides on a string round a horizontal circle on the ice, seen from the side; the string and the centre of the circle are on the left. The diagram shows only the puck as a rectangle on the ice. The weight G from the centre downwards. The support force N of the ice from the bottom face upwards and equally long. The tension T of the string from the middle of the left side horizontally to the left towards the centre, a little under half the length of the weight. Separately the orange acceleration arrow a n to the left. In the corner the axes: x to the left towards the centre and y up.
Vuoristoradan vaunun voimakuvio, vaunu s: Free-body diagram of a roller coaster car, the car drawn as a rectangle. The weight G points down from the centre. The support force N coming from below points straight up and ends at the bottom face; it is half the length of the weight.

Free-body diagram of a roller coaster car, the car drawn as a rectangle. The weight G points down from the centre. The support force N coming from above points straight down and ends at the top face; it is half the length of the weight. From the left side of the top face an arrow F cf goes straight up, one and a half times the length of the weight.

Free-body diagram of a roller coaster car, the car drawn as a rectangle. The weight G points down from the centre. The support force N coming from above points straight down and ends at the top face; it is half the length of the weight.

Free-body diagram of a roller coaster car, the car drawn as a rectangle. The weight G points down from the centre. The support force N coming from above points straight down and ends at the top face; it is half the length of the weight. From the right side a blue velocity arrow v goes horizontally to the right, as long as the support force.
Kuvaaja mittakaavassa: auton normaalikii: Graph to scale: the centripetal acceleration a n of a car in metres per second squared as a function of its speed v in a bend. On the horizontal axis the speed goes from zero to 30 metres per second, with gridlines and numbers every five; on the vertical axis the acceleration goes from zero to 12, with gridlines every one and numbers every two. An orange curve rises from the origin ever more steeply. A point is marked on the curve with guide lines: at speed 20 the centripetal acceleration is 5.
Kuvaaja mittakaavassa: kaarteessa ajavan: Graph to scale: the friction force F a car driving in a bend needs, in kilonewtons, as a function of its speed v. On the horizontal axis the speed goes from zero to 25 metres per second, with gridlines and numbers every five; on the vertical axis the force goes from zero to 12 kilonewtons, with gridlines every one and numbers every two. A red curve rises from the origin ever more steeply. A point is marked on the curve with guide lines: at speed 20 the force is 8.
